terms.gloss: scent out, have a nose for, get wind of
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.14.2: solēs enim tū haec fēstīvē odōrārī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 104: to have a good nose for these things, haec fēstīvē odōrārī
terms.comment: Of a hound first, then of people who sniff out what is going on: Cicero has quid futūrum sit (Att. 14.22.1), what is going to happen. Fēstīvē adds “cleverly, nicely”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 104, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
